items.name: block-no-verify-hook
items.author: wshobson
items.description: Stop AI coding agents from bypassing git pre-commit hooks, formatting, linting, and security checks.
items.summary: Block-no-verify hook is a PreToolUse configuration guard that intercepts Bash tool calls from AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) and rejects commands containing bypass flags like --no-verify and --no-gpg-sign before execution. Developers use it when setting up agent-driven projects to enforce commit quality gates, linting, formatting, security scanning, and GPG signing policies. The hook inspects every shell command via regex pattern matching against $TOOL_INPUT, exits with code 2 to block the tool call if a bypass flag is detected, or code 0 to allow normal execution. Installation is per-project (.claude/settings.json) or global (~/.claude/settings.json). The configuration is extendable to block additional dangerous flags. PreToolUse hook matcher targets only Bash calls without interfering with Read, Edit, or Grep tools. Blocks --no-verify and --no-gpg-sign flags via grep regex pattern inspection of $TOOL_INPUT. Exit code 2 signal rejects tool call entirely; exit code 0 allows normal execution. Installable per-project or globally; works alongside other PreToolUse hooks in same configuration. Extendable pattern to block additional dangerous flags like --force or --force-with-lea.
highlights: PreToolUse hook matcher targets only Bash calls without interfering with Read, Edit, or Grep tools.
Blocks --no-verify and --no-gpg-sign flags via grep regex pattern inspection of $TOOL_INPUT.
Exit code 2 signal rejects tool call entirely; exit code 0 allows normal execution.
Installable per-project or globally; works alongside other PreToolUse hooks in same configuration.
Extendable pattern to block additional dangerous flags like --force or --force-with-lease.

Tasks are declarative YAML files specifying actions, files touched, and deterministic judges for success. Each agent run gets an isolated git worktree without Docker so agents cannot interfere with each other or corrupt the base repository. Collected metrics include pass rate against judges, API cost per task when available, wall-clock completion time, and consistency across repeated trials such as three-of-three passes. Workflow creates a tasks directory, runs agents against tasks, generates comparison reports, and supports judge types: codebase deterministic tests, pattern-based checks, and optional LLM-as-judge with caution about noise. Best practices recommend starting with three to five real workload tasks, at least three trials per agent, pinning task YAML commits for reproducibility, including at least one deterministic judge per task, tracking cost alongside pass rate, and versioning task definitions like test fixtures.

items.name: content-quality-auditor
items.author: aaron-he-zhu
items.description: Run systematic CORE-EEAT audits on landing pages, blog posts, and documentation before publishing.
items.summary: The content-quality-auditor skill scores articles and landing pages against the CORE-EEAT benchmark before publish or after major edits from seo-content-writer or geo-content-optimizer. It runs a full 80-item audit with Pass, Partial, or Fail ratings across eight dimensions, computes GEO and SEO system scores, applies content-type-specific weights, and flags veto violations such as critical trust failures. Outputs include dimension scores, weighted totals, top five priority improvements sorted by impact, and an actionable fix plan with a publish verdict plus handoff summary in the repository skill-contract format. The skill triggers when users ask if content is ready to publish, request E-E-A-T analysis, or when post-edit hooks recommend a quality gate. It is for quality and trust scoring, not structural on-page tag audits or domain authority reviews covered by sibling skills. Agents should skip setup questions when hook-triggered and audit the content just produced. Use when benchmarking drafts against CORE-EEAT or comparing competitor content quality.
highlights: Scores all 80 CORE-EEAT items across eight dimensions with Pass, Partial, or Fail ratings.
Computes GEO and SEO system scores with content-type-specific weighted totals.
Detects veto violations for critical trust failures before publish approval.
Ranks top five improvements by impact and outputs a concrete fix plan.
Pairs with seo-content-writer and geo-content-optimizer as the publish-readiness gate.

items.name: seo-plan
items.author: AgriciDaniel
items.description: Generate a complete, industry-specific SEO strategy including competitive analysis, site architecture, content calendar, and implementation roadmap.
items.summary: seo-plan is an AgriciDaniel claude-seo skill at version 2.2.0 for strategic SEO planning on new or existing websites. The process runs discovery on business type, audience, competitors, goals, current site assessment, budget, timeline, and KPIs, then competitive analysis on top five rivals covering content, schema, technical setup, keyword gaps, and E-E-A-T signals. Architecture design loads industry templates from assets for SaaS, local service, ecommerce, publisher, agency, or generic businesses, planning URL hierarchy, content pillars, internal linking, and sitemap quality gates. Content strategy defines gaps, page types, publishing cadence, and author credibility plans. Technical foundation covers hosting, schema per page type, Core Web Vitals targets, AI search readiness, and mobile-first requirements. A four-phase roadmap spans foundation weeks one to four, expansion weeks five to twelve, scale weeks thirteen to twenty-four, and authority months seven to twelve. Deliverables include SEO-STRATEGY.md, COMPETITOR-ANALYSIS.md, CONTENT-CALENDAR.md, IMPLEMENTATION-ROADMAP.md, and SITE-STRUCTURE.md.

items.name: microinteractions
items.author: wondelai
items.description: Get ready-to-implement blueprints for common UI microinteractions that feel polished and intuitive.
items.summary: Microinteractions are small, contained product moments built around single use cases that users rarely think about consciously but feel every day. Based on Dan Saffer's four-part framework, this skill teaches designers to craft triggers (how interactions start), rules (what happens), feedback (what users see/hear), and loops/modes (how behavior evolves). Master the six design areas: triggers, rules, feedback, loops and modes, signature moments, and reduction. Covers button states, form validation, loading indicators, toggle controls, pull-to-refresh, and state transitions. Includes common mistakes, quick diagnostics, and case studies for real-world application.
highlights: Four-part structure: Trigger, Rules, Feedback, Loops & Modes
10/10 scoring system to audit and improve microinteractions systematically
Progressive reduction: strip scaffolding as users demonstrate mastery
Signature moments: distinctive microinteractions that become product identity
Ethical boundaries: honest feedback, transparent rules, user-first loops
